ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Primary AML/CFT statute: Law No. 80 of 2002 on Combating Money Laundering, as amended, including amendments introduced by Laws No. 78 of 2003, 181 of 2008, 36 of 2014, 8 of 2015, 64 of 2017 and subsequent amendments. Executive framework: Prime Ministerial Decree No. 951 of 2003 issuing the Executive Regulations of Law No. 80 of 2002, as amended. Corporate ownership and control records: Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 and its Executive Regulations issued by Prime Ministerial Decree No. 96 of 1982, as amended. Customs and bonded-warehouse controls: Customs Law No. 207 of 2020 and its implementing regulations. Investment and free-zone framework: Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 and its Executive Regulations issued by Prime Ministerial Decree No. 2310 of 2017. Egypt requires regulated institutions and relevant businesses to identify and verify the natural person who ultimately owns or controls the customer, including through ownership, voting rights, management control or other effective control. Egypt does not operate a generally searchable public beneficial-ownership register equivalent to the United Kingdom register; disclosure is primarily to competent authorities, the Financial Intelligence Unit, tax authorities, customs authorities, licensing bodies and regulated reporting entities. No single publicly verified standalone UBO-register decree should be relied upon without confirming the current GAFI, AML Unit and Commercial Registry requirements.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before incorporation, banking, licensing and each material transaction, screen all shareholders, directors, managers, authorized signatories, UBOs, suppliers, customers, freight counterparties and agents against United Nations Security Council sanctions, United States OFAC lists, applicable European Union and United Kingdom lists, Egyptian domestic sanctions and terrorism lists, and reputable PEP, RCA, adverse-media and law-enforcement databases. Apply enhanced due diligence to PEPs, close associates, high-risk jurisdictions, cash-intensive activity, opaque ownership, unusual shipping routes, sanctioned goods and free-zone or customs transactions. Obtain source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence, document escalation decisions, apply sanctions blocking or rejection where legally required, and file suspicious transaction reports with the Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit where the reporting obligation is triggered. OFAC and other foreign lists may be commercially relevant even where not independently binding on an Egyptian entity.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_piercing_methodology: Trace ownership through every legal entity, nominee, trust, partnership and voting arrangement to natural persons. Test direct and indirect ownership, voting rights, appointment rights, veto rights, contractual control, financing dependence, family or concert-party arrangements and de facto management. Do not accept a nominee, professional director or senior managing official as the UBO unless reasonable documentary investigation fails to identify a controlling natural person and the residual senior-official rule is properly documented.
enhanced_risk_factors_for_target_activit: Bonded warehouses and free zones involve customs-controlled goods, transit activity and potential trade-based money-laundering exposure.
Third-party logistics, freight forwarding, cash-equivalent goods, complex invoices, under-invoicing, over-invoicing and diversion to sanctioned destinations require enhanced transaction monitoring.

The company should maintain customer acceptance criteria, shipment-level sanctions screening, beneficial-owner verification for cargo owners and counterparties, customs-document reconciliation and segregation of duties.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) electronic incorporation and name-reservation services, accessed through the official GAFI portal at https://www.gafi.gov.eg; Commercial Registry services are administered through the Internal Trade Development Authority and relevant Commercial Registry offices
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be available, distinguishable and compliant with Egyptian Companies Law No. 159 of 1981, its Executive Regulations and GAFI filing rules. Arabic is required for the official Arabic corporate name and governmental filings. A foreign-language or transliterated name may be used as an additional commercial presentation only if accepted by GAFI and not misleading. The name must not conflict with an existing registered name, trademark, governmental institution, public authority, regulated activity or public order. The legal form designation, such as Limited Liability Company or its accepted Arabic equivalent, must be reflected in the constitutional documents and registration.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Any religious, military, sovereign or governmental designation
Any term implying a regulated financial, insurance, customs, port or governmental function without the required sectoral approval
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Obtain the written or electronic rejection reason from GAFI or the Commercial Registry. Confirm whether the issue concerns similarity, prohibited terminology, trademark conflict, Arabic wording, legal-form wording or missing sectoral approval. File a corrected name application within the reservation system where permitted. For an adverse administrative decision, submit a reasoned reconsideration request to the issuing GAFI or Commercial Registry office, attaching alternative names, trademark clearance, corporate documents and any required ministerial or sectoral approval. If the decision is maintained, escalate through the competent administrative grievance channel and, where legally justified, pursue judicial review before the Egyptian State Council. Do not use the rejected name in contracts, banking or licensing applications pending clearance.
recommended_name_clearance_sequence: Conduct GAFI and Commercial Registry similarity searches.
Conduct Egyptian trademark searches with the Internal Trade Development Authority and assess Arabic and Latin-script conflicts.
Obtain preliminary sectoral clearance if the proposed name contains regulated or governmental terminology.
Reserve the name before signing long-term premises, customs or banking commitments.
Preserve the reservation certificate and submit incorporation documents within the applicable reservation window.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A registered address in Egypt is required for company registration and official service. A serviced or virtual office may be accepted as a registered administrative address if the provider, lease, premises evidence and governmental inspection requirements are acceptable to GAFI, the Commercial Registry, tax authority and licensing bodies. It is not sufficient for the operational activity of a bonded warehouse, customs warehouse, depot or free-zone logistics facility. The company must have an approved physical warehouse or depot, customs controls, appropriate lease or title evidence, fire and safety approvals, inventory systems, responsible personnel and any SCZone, GAFI, customs or port authority authorization applicable to the location.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Indicative risk: 60-85 percent before or during licensing for a bonded warehouse or customs-controlled depot, and 20-40 percent for a conventional administrative registration address. These are risk estimates rather than statutory probabilities. Unannounced or follow-up inspections may be initiated by Customs, GAFI, the tax authority, the relevant free-zone authority, port authorities, civil defense or other competent regulators, particularly where the applicant handles high-value goods, regulated goods, third-party cargo, transit shipments or material foreign payments.
commercial_substance_requirements: Maintain a genuine Egyptian management and operations function proportionate to the licensed activity.
Maintain a physical facility capable of receiving, securing, identifying and releasing bonded goods under customs supervision.
Maintain Arabic-capable regulatory records, customs documentation, inventory ledgers, contracts, invoices, transport documents and inspection records.
Appoint accountable managers and authorized representatives with documented authority and fit-and-proper records.
Maintain local accounting, tax, payroll and AML records and ensure consistency among GAFI, Commercial Registry, tax, customs, banking and licensing data.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Egyptian Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 (as amended), Arts. 1-7, 9-27, and 54-68; Investment Law No. 72 of 2017, Art. 31 and Executive Regulations; Commercial Registration Law No. 34/1976
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) – Investor Services Center and Commercial Registry Department
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum and Articles of Association (Incorporation Contract) and Application for Establishment (Form FA-1)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for LLC under Companies Law 159/1981. Free-zone projects require capital adequacy review by GAFI; no escrow account is mandatory, but paid-up capital must be evidenced by a bank certificate upon filing.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: That the incorporators hereby subscribe to the shares of the Company in accordance with the Memorandum of Association; that the registered office of the Company is adopted at Plot [X], Zone [Y], Suez Canal Economic Zone, Egypt; that the following individuals are appointed as directors: [Name] – CEO, [Name] – CFO, [Name] – Company Secretary; that the board is authorized to undertake all filings with GAFI and the Commercial Registry, to open bank accounts, and to engage licensed agents for the purpose of obtaining the Free Zone Project License and bonded warehouse operating permits. Further resolved that the directors are empowered to execute all ancillary documents and to sign the first financial statements.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Legal Form Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI – Investor Services Center (online via www.gafi.gov.eg)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the GAFI One-Stop Shop portal, create an investor profile, submit up to three proposed company names with preferred transliteration and legal form 'Limited Liability Company'. Pay the name reservation fee by card. Print the reservation certificate.
required_dossiers: Investor identity documents (passport or national ID)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for similarity, the applicant may propose up to two further names within 3 business days; appeal to GAFI Legal Directorate if the name conflicts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian General Directorate of Notarization (Ministry of Justice)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the drafted Memorandum and Articles of Association to notary public office with jurisdiction over the registered office address. Ensure all founding members sign in person after verification of legal capacity. Notary authenticates signatures and affixes official seal.
required_dossiers: Proof of registered office (lease contract or ownership deed)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary issues a correction request, amend the contract in accordance with the Companies Law and resubmit; notarial refusal may be appealed in the Court of First Instance within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI – Company Registration Window / One-Stop Shop
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the notarized incorporation contract and supporting documents into the GAFI electronic system; schedule an in-person appointment at the Investor Services Center for biometric verification of founding partners. Pay the official state fees through the system and obtain the incorporation decision (electronic incorporation certificate).
required_dossiers: Bank certificate confirming paid-up capital deposit
Lease or ownership deed for the registered office
Board resolution regarding subscriptions and officers (as attached)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI issues a query or request for information, address it in writing within 15 business days; missing documents can be submitted via the portal; failure to respond results in deemed refusal, subject to administrative review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registry Office (Ministry of Trade and Industry) and Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After GAFI issuance, the company is automatically registered in the Commercial Registry. Visit ETA with the commercial registry extract to obtain the Tax Identification Card and mandatory VAT/Stamp registration; also register the physical depot for import/export purposes.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: For tax card delays, request expeditious issuance via the ETA investor support unit; if the commercial extract contains errors, submit a correction request to the Commercial Registry within 10 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Free Zone Project License and Bonded Depot Permit Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI – Free Zones Administration in coordination with Egyptian Customs Authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Free Zone project application with GAFI Free Zones Administration. Provide project description, capital plan, and floor plan of the depot. Upon approval, obtain the Free Zone Operating License and apply separately to Customs for the bonded warehouse permit. Comply with the reserved area and duties suspension rules.
required_dossiers: Environmental clearance and civil defense approval (as per licensing section)
Commercial registry extract and tax card
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the free zone license is refused, request a hearing before the GAFI Board of Directors; for the customs permit, appeal to the Minister of Finance within 30 days; rectify plan deficiencies and resubmit.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: GAFI – Free Zones Administration (General Authority for Investment and Free Zones) in coordination with Egyptian Customs Authority (Bonded Warehouse Directorate)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Free Zone Project License – Bonded Warehouse Operations (Customs Bonded Warehouse License issued by Egyptian Customs Authority)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B – Limited Environmental Registration (Low-to-Moderate Risk), completed through the Integrated Environmental Management System
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Law No. 4/1994 (as amended): zero direct discharge of untreated wastewater to the water body; VOC emissions below 30 mg/m3 in working environment; waste handling per Waste Management Law No. 202/2020 and storage segregation requirements for bonded goods.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Civil Defense Authority (structural inspections, fire suppression system, emergency exits); structural load certification from the municipal engineering directorate; workplace clearance from the Ministry of Manpower covering warehouse occupational safety standards.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) – Ministry of Finance; official portals: www.eta.gov.eg and the ETA e-invoicing/e-tax platform at invoicing.eta.gov.eg
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Egyptian LLC must first complete commercial registration with the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) or the Ministry of Trade and Industry, then file the unified tax file (maalf al-sharika) with the competent ETA office. Submit legalized articles of association in Arabic, commercial registry extract, contract/lease for registered premises, board resolution appointing a fiscal representative, director passport copies, power of attorney, and opening balance sheet. The ETA issues a single Tax Identification Number (TIN) used for income tax, VAT, stamp duty, and payroll. For a free-zone bonded depot, the operator additionally obtains a free-zone license from GAFI/SCZONE and receives a free-zone project file number; a separate customs bonded-warehouse license is issued by the Egyptian Customs Authority. The ETA account is then activated for e-filing and e-invoicing API credentials.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — an Egyptian-resident limited liability company is a juridical person taxed at entity level on Egyptian-source income and worldwide income if fully resident; free-zone bonded-depot projects are, by special statute, treated as taxable under the Investment Law free-zone fee regime rather than ordinary CIT/VAT for approved physical operations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Egyptian law does not provide a US-style 'check-the-box' election or hybrid mismatch election. Available statutory elections include: (i) election through GAFI/SCZONE to operate a project in a free trade zone, replacing full corporate income tax, VAT, customs and stamp duties with an annual gross-revenue fee (generally 1%) on free-zone operations; (ii) election of the simplified small and medium enterprise (SME) gross-receipts tax regime where annual turnover is within the statutory threshold; (iii) election to file on a fiscal-year basis by obtaining ETA approval; and (iv) for groups, electing consolidated tax filing where all legal conditions are met. Pass-through treatment is not an available election for an LLC.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value Added Tax) under Law No. 67 of 2016, as amended by the Unified Tax Law No. 22 of 2025 and implemented by the ETA; Egyptian customs duties apply separately under Customs Law No. 207 of 2020
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Mandatory ETA VAT registration is triggered when annual taxable supplies exceed EGP 500,000; voluntary registration is possible above EGP 250,000 annual turnover. A licensed free-zone bonded depot is not subject to ordinary VAT registration for in-zone/re-export operations; it must instead be entered in the ETA free-zone project fee registry and register for import VAT when goods are cleared into the national customs territory.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Egypt mandates real-time e-invoicing and e-receipts through the Egyptian E-Invoice System (EIS). All registered taxpayers must issue B2B invoices as structured XML or PDF through ETA-certified ERP/API integrations, obtain an ETA-generated unique identifier (UUID) and QR 'fiscal stamp' before releasing invoices to customers, and transmit the invoice to the ETA for automated clearance. The ETA cross-matches invoice data with customs declarations and banking transfer records. Free-zone companies selling into the national market, or issuing documents for the annual fee calculation, must comply with the same e-invoicing protocols; failure to clear invoices in real time invalidates input VAT deduction and incurs statutory penalties.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to goods physically exported outside Egypt and to certain international transport and related services. For free-zone bonded depots, goods entering the licensed depot for storage and subsequent re-export are treated as being outside the Egyptian VAT/customs territory; in practice the movement out of Egypt, or the supply into a free-zone bonded warehouse, is considered an export supply on which the 0% VAT rate (or full out-of-scope treatment) applies. The operator must prove that the goods actually left Egypt, that they entered customs-bonded storage under customs supervision, and that they were not diverted into the domestic market.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (final SAD / export declaration form)
Free-zone entry declaration or customs receipt evidencing deposit into the bonded depot
Bill of Lading (or Air Waybill / multimodal transport document)
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) issued by an Egyptian bank evidencing receipt of foreign-currency export proceeds
Certificate of Origin, insurance certificate, and customs warehouse stock ledger extracts (when applicable)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The ETA and Egyptian Customs jointly audit export declarations, free-zone stock reports, and banking confirmations. Any unjustified zero-rating or input VAT refund obtained through false export declarations, forged documents, failure to re-export within the free-zone timeline, or diversion to the domestic market is clawed back with VAT plus late payment interest at 2% per month, a fine of 100% to 300% of the evaded tax, and potential criminal liability including imprisonment. The free-zone license may be suspended or revoked, and the 1% annual gross-revenue fee may be reassessed on the full value of goods cleared for local consumption.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) under Law No. 194 of 2020 (Central Bank and Banking System Law); CBE Board circulars govern the foreign exchange market, authorised dealer banks, and balance-of-payments reporting. The General Authority for Investment (GAFI) supports the foreign-investment file, while customs-duty and bonded-depot supervision sit with the Egyptian Customs Authority.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt operates a market-determined, flexible exchange-rate regime following the March 2024 liberalisation, with the interbank USD/EGP rate set daily by CBE-authorized dealers. Current-account transactions (trade settlements, service fees, dividend remittances) are generally permitted through the banking system against underlying documentation. Profit remittance requires audited financial statements, a tax clearance certificate confirming settlement of corporate tax and withholding tax, and CBE-registered foreign capital evidentiary documents. Capital-account movements (intercompany loans, guarantees, outward investment) require CBE registration or approval. Free-zone bonded-depot operators enjoy streamlined treatment on trade-linked currency flows, but full convertibility is conditional on documentary compliance and the absence of foreign-currency rationing during periods of balance-of-payments pressure.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds must be repatriated to an Egyptian licensed bank and credited within 90 days from the bill-of-lading date (extendable to 180 days with CBE approval for specific sectors). Under the post-March-2024 floating regime, 100% of export receipts must pass through the domestic banking system; the CBE instructs banks to mandatorily convert the proceeds into EGP at prevailing market rates, with retention in foreign currency permitted only up to documented future import or hard-currency tax/expense obligations and subject to bank compliance approval. The bonded warehouse must therefore structure receivable collections to clear via Egyptian authorised banks, with conversion timing aligned to weekly inventory-turnover cash flow to minimise translation exposure.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account; EGP Operational Account; Foreign-Currency Account (USD/EUR) for trade settlements
Capital Escrow Account; EGP Operational Account; Foreign-Currency Account for LC-backed imports
EGP Operational Account; Foreign-Currency Account; dedicated treasury coverage for FX forwards and swaps
EGP Operational Account; multi-currency current account; trade-finance and correspondent USD clearing desk
EGP Operational Account; Foreign-Currency Account; bonded-hardware trade settlement facilities

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low for settlement-grade treasury purposes. Non-resident digital EMIs (e.g., Wise, Airwallex, Payoneer) hold no CBE banking licence and cannot maintain corporate EGP accounts, issue letters of credit, or provide clearing rails into the Egyptian RTGS system. Under Law 18 of 2019 (Payments Law) and Law 194 of 2020, deposit-taking and foreign-exchange dealing are restricted to CBE-licensed banks. A non-resident EMI may only function as a front-end payment aggregator partnered with a licensed Egyptian bank, and is unsuitable as the primary clearing or FX execution platform for this bonded-depot entity.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is mandated for corporate account opening at all CBE-licensed tier-1 banks. All authorised signatories and each natural-person ultimate beneficial owner (or their locally resident attorney-in-fact holding a notarised, apostilled power of attorney) must appear at the branch for biometric identity verification, wet-ink signatures, and a compliance interview. Remote or video-only onboarding is not accepted for first-time corporate relationships; documentary pre-review by email is permitted, but original certified documentation and in-person execution remain compulsory. For foreign directors, certified true copies of passports, apostilled board resolutions, and GAFI registration certificates must be presented in Arabic or with certified Arabic translation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incomplete Ultimate Beneficial Ownership (UBO) disclosure, defined as any natural person directly or indirectly holding 10% or more, or exercising control, not evidenced to bank satisfaction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised UBO declaration on the CBE-prescribed form; extract from the GAFI-certified shareholders register; certified memorandum and articles of association; passport copies of all UBOs and signatories; written confirmation that no nominee or bearer-share arrangement exists; bank-format beneficial-ownership attestation executed by the managing director.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border FDI remittance flagged during sanctions or source-of-funds screening, particularly where the remitter jurisdiction or intermediary corridor raises enhanced-due-diligence alerts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Subscription or shareholder-loan agreement; board resolutions approving the FDI injection; audited financial statements of the foreign investor; bank statements of the remitting entity evidencing historical accumulation of funds; independent legal opinion on economic substance; completed CBE Enhanced Due Diligence questionnaire; declaration of absence of sanctioned-jurisdiction links and PEP exposure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Free-zone bonded-depot licence and customs authorisation not yet validated by the bank's compliance section, creating uncertainty over the declared Medium-Risk Enhanced trade profile.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: GAFI free-zone establishment licence for the bonded depot; Egyptian Customs Authority bonded-warehouse operational permit; ISIC 5210 scope description and warehouse operating plan; AML/CTF internal manual demonstrating client-asset segregation and transaction monitoring; valid taxpayer card and tax clearance certificate; list of bonded inventory categories and custody procedures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Import-payment instructions referencing high-risk jurisdictions or unusual intermediary routes, generating a wire-transparency red flag under the bank's trade-based money-laundering controls.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial invoice and proforma contract; bill of lading; NAFIZA/ACID customs declaration number; declared CBE import-form reference or documentary-credit instrument; complete correspondent-bank chain disclosure; attestation of non-involvement of shell or unlicensed intermediaries; sworn declaration of genuine bonded-depot end-use.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign director or shareholder identified as a politically exposed person (PEP), which in a free-zone trade entity may trigger refusal or prolonged enhanced monitoring.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PEP status declaration executed by the affected individual; independent source-of-wealth report prepared by a licensed professional; reputable international counsel confirmation of the entity's commercial substance; verified management accounts and warehouse throughput evidence; approval memorandum from the bank's Money Laundering Reporting Officer documenting risk acceptance and periodic review.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Foreign equity injection must be routed by SWIFT MT103 over the correspondent network into the LLC's CBE-licensed beneficiary bank. The remitter must annotate the wire with the CBE balance-of-payments purpose classification for foreign direct investment (equity capital) and the GAFI investment-file number. The beneficiary bank opens a Capital Escrow Account, verifies the underlying subscription agreement and board resolution, and files the inward FDI declaration with the CBE statistical department so that future dividend repatriation and capital liquidation can be sourced from documented FDI proceeds. Supporting verification comprises apostilled certificate of incorporation of the foreign investor, UBO disclosure, source-of-funds evidence, and the Egyptian LLC's commercial registration and certificate of commencement; settlement through an unlicensed intermediary, cryptocurrency, or non-correspondent shell account is not permitted.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements for the bonded depot's import and working-capital payments are executed via SWIFT MT103 for open-account supplier payments and via MT700/MT707 commercial documentary credits under UCP600 for goods requiring bank confirmation. All Egyptian goods imports require registration on the NAFIZA platform with a valid ACID number and a bank-approved CBE import form or trade-finance instrument before remittance. Domestic EGP obligations (customs duties, municipal fees, local logistics) clear through the CBE RTGS system and the Instant Payment Network (IPN). USD liquidity is obtained on the interbank FX market at market rates, with same-day USD settlement available for confirmed trade invoices. Standby letters of credit under ISP98 are acceptable as collateral enhancement for bank-issued guarantees.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable onshore FX forward contracts (USD/EGP and EUR/EGP) with tenors up to 12 months, provided the exposure is supported by genuine trade invoices or bonded inventory purchase contracts validated by the executing bank
Offshore nondeliverable forward contracts (NDF) on EGP for non-resident hedging partners, settled in USD or EUR offshore to align with cross-border supplier and buyer hedge books

Cross-currency swaps (USD/EGP and EUR/EGP) executed through CBE-licensed treasury desks for matching long-term asset-liability currency exposure, subject to underlying trade or capital-documentation evidence and CBE transaction filing
Onshore FX swaps (EGP/USD or EGP/EUR, both legs settled in Egypt) for short-term working-capital conversion aligned with import-payment cycles and export-receipt conversion

Purchased, non-leveraged FX option contracts (USD/EGP or EUR/EGP) for protection against adverse trade-cost movements, with the writing bank retaining discretion based on the customer's demonstrated underlying exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Tax Form No. 123)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months after tax year-end; no later than 30 April for a 31 December accounting period.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 2% monthly late-filing and underpayment penalty on outstanding tax; additional fixed fines EGP 500–5,000; continued default triggers forced assessment, asset seizure, and eventual administrative strike-off via GAFI.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited Annual Financial Statements and Directors' Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) and General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Simultaneously with the annual corporate income tax return; by 30 April for calendar-year LLCs.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Rejection of the tax return; 1% monthly delinquency fine on unpaid tax; suspension of free-zone incentives; two consecutive years of non-filing leads to GAFI strike-off and license revocation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry, Ministry of Trade and Industry (via GAFI)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary of the original commercial registration date; renewal may be made 60 days before expiry.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late penalty EGP 150 per month; registry suspension after 3 months; administrative strike-off after 6 months of non-renewal.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership (UBO) Confirmation and Register Update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA) – UBO/AML Digital Portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 January following the reporting calendar year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to EGP 2,000,000 for inaccurate UBO filing; daily penalty EGP 5,000; prohibition against dividend distribution; possible court-ordered removal of directors.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Free Zone / Bonded Depot Annual Licence Renewal (Warehouse Customs Bond)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) and Egyptian Customs Authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days preceding the licence anniversary date, generally aligned with the commercial registration renewal.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Immediate cessation of bonded-warehouse privileges; customs bond enforcement; administrative fines up to EGP 100,000; GAFI strike-off if renewal is not completed within 90 days after expiry.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Compulsory independent audit is required for all Egyptian LLCs holding a free-zone bonded depot license, irrespective of turnover. In addition, audit is mandatory if issued capital exceeds EGP 50,000, if the number of partners exceeds ten, or if annual turnover exceeds EGP 20,000,000 under Egyptian Companies Law No. 194 of 2020.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), substantially converged with IFRS for entities exceeding small-enterprise thresholds; full IFRS is mandatory for banks and listed entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each LLC must file an annual UBO confirmation with the Egyptian Financial Regulatory Authority before 31 January for the preceding calendar year. Any direct or indirect shareholding transfer of 10% or more must be reported to the UBO portal within 30 days, with a notarized transfer instrument and updated register extract; failure to do so invalidates the transfer for corporate-law purposes and attracts fines up to EGP 2,000,000.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 350 – USD 1,200 per year for a licensed registered office in Cairo or a free-zone administrative address; registered agent services range from USD 500 – USD 1,800 per year.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,500 – USD 3,500 per year for an LLC operating a bonded warehouse with moderate transaction volume and calendar-year financials.
